review_notes: Read the whole file, Mathlib DSlope.lean (variables: 𝕜 NontriviallyNormedField, E normed space over 𝕜), IsolatedZeros.lean (has_fpower_series_dslope_fslope, iterate lemma stated over general 𝕜, E; no completeness needed), and Deriv/Mul and Slope lemma statements. Every Mathlib lemma used in the file is already stated for a general nontrivially normed field, so ℂ is never used essentially (no Complex-specific lemma appears). Checked usage counts in other files in lean-pool (37 occurrences in 7 files) but did not verify that all downstream users would be unaffected; since specialisation to ℂ would be recovered by instantiating 𝕜 := ℂ, they should be. I have not compiled any proposed changes; the proposed changes for the field-generalisation rely on the used Mathlib lemmas (Finset.analyticAt_fun_sum, HasFPowerSeriesAt.add, analyticAt_const, fun_prop) being available at general 𝕜, which I did not exhaustively verify (the last two are typically general).

findings.declaration: RS.taylorCoeffAt (and the whole ℂ-specialised development, e.g. AnalyticAt.iterate_dslope, HasFPowerSeriesAt.taylorCoeffAt_eq, taylorCoeffAt_add, taylorCoeffAt_sub_pow_mul, AnalyticAt.exists_taylor_remainder)
findings.excerpt:
noncomputable def taylorCoeffAt (g : ℂ → ℂ) (z₀ : ℂ) (j : ℕ) : ℂ :=
  (Function.swap dslope z₀)^[j] g z₀
findings.problem: The definition and every theorem is fixed to ℂ → ℂ, yet nothing is complex-specific: `dslope`, `slope`, `deriv`, `HasFPowerSeriesAt.has_fpower_series_iterate_dslope_fslope`, `FormalMultilinearSeries.coeff_iterate_fslope`, `pow_sub_smul_iterate_dslope_of_zero` are all stated for `[NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜]` (and the dslope/power-series ones for `E` a normed space over 𝕜). The only proof-level uses of ℂ are the `AnalyticAt ℂ`/`HasFPowerSeriesAt` binders and `FormalMultilinearSeries ℂ ℂ ℂ`. This forces users over ℝ (or ℂ-valued maps from ℝ-style 𝕜, p-adic fields, vector-valued functions) to re-develop the same API.
findings.proposed_change: Replace `ℂ` by a variable `{𝕜 : Type*} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜]` (and, for the definition and the lemmas that only use dslope/power-series bridge, optionally a codomain `{E} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E]`): `noncomputable def taylorCoeffAt (g : 𝕜 → E) (z₀ : 𝕜) (j : ℕ) : E := (Function.swap dslope z₀)^[j] g z₀`. Then `AnalyticAt.iterate_dslope`, `HasFPowerSeriesAt.taylorCoeffAt_eq` (with `p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 𝕜 E`), `taylorCoeffAt_congr`, `taylorCoeffAt_add`, `_fun_sum` go through unchanged (same Mathlib lemmas, which are already stated over 𝕜, E). The multiplicative lemmas (`_const_mul`, `_sub_pow_mul`, `_monomial`, `exists_taylor_remainder`) can be stated for `g : 𝕜 → 𝕜` over any nontrivially normed field (or with `•` for E-valued g, using `dslope_sub_smul_of_ne` as the proof of `dslope_sub_mul` already does). Specialising to ℂ is then just `𝕜 := ℂ`.
findings.benefit: The same Taylor-coefficient API becomes usable for real-analytic, vector-valued and non-archimedean settings, and the file's statements match the generality of the Mathlib lemmas they wrap, with no additional mathematics.

findings.excerpt:
theorem Filter.EventuallyEq.dslope_eq (hfg : f =ᶠ[𝓝 z₀] g) :
    dslope f z₀ =ᶠ[𝓝 z₀] dslope g z₀ := by
findings.problem: This is a general fact about `dslope`, but is stated only for `f g : ℂ → ℂ`. The proof only uses `dslope_same`, `dslope_of_ne`, `EventuallyEq.deriv_eq`, and unfolding `slope`; the `slope_def_field` rewrites (which force a field codomain) are the only place the codomain is used, and they can be replaced by unfolding `slope` (`slope f a b = (b - a)⁻¹ • (f b - f a)`), which rewrites with `hb`, `hz` equally well.
findings.proposed_change: State it with `{𝕜 E} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] {f g : 𝕜 → E} {z₀ : 𝕜}`: `theorem Filter.EventuallyEq.dslope_eq (hfg : f =ᶠ[𝓝 z₀] g) : dslope f z₀ =ᶠ[𝓝 z₀] dslope g z₀`. Proof sketch: same case split; in the `b ≠ z₀` case use `rw [dslope_of_ne _ hbz, dslope_of_ne _ hbz, slope, slope]` (or `simp only [slope_def_module]`) followed by `rw [hb, hz]`; the `b = z₀` case is unchanged (`dslope_same`, `hfg.deriv_eq`, which is already general).
findings.benefit: A reusable, Mathlib-style lemma about `dslope` (a candidate for Mathlib's DSlope file) that is applicable to real/vector-valued functions and not tied to this ℂ-valued file; also makes the ℂ version a special case.

findings.excerpt:
theorem dslope_const_mul (c : ℂ) (g : ℂ → ℂ) (z₀ : ℂ) :
    dslope (fun z => c * g z) z₀ = fun b => c * dslope g z₀ b := by
findings.problem: These are generic identities about `dslope` but are stated only over ℂ. The proofs use `deriv_const_mul_field`, `slope_def_field`, `ring` and `simp`, which are all valid over any nontrivially normed field; `dslope_const` is even valid for constants valued in any normed space E (`dslope (fun _ : 𝕜 => c) a = fun _ => 0`, using `slope_fun_def`/`simp`). Likewise `dslope_sub_mul` (line 156) uses `hasDerivAt_id`, `HasDerivAt.mul` and `dslope_sub_smul_of_ne`, all general.
findings.proposed_change: Declare `{𝕜 : Type*} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜]` and state `dslope_const_mul (c : 𝕜) (g : 𝕜 → 𝕜) (z₀ : 𝕜)`, `dslope_const {E} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] (c : E) (z₀ : 𝕜) : dslope (fun _ : 𝕜 => c) z₀ = fun _ => 0`, and `dslope_sub_mul {F : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (hF : DifferentiableAt 𝕜 F z₀) : dslope (fun z => (z - z₀) * F z) z₀ = F`. The existing proofs should carry over verbatim since `deriv_const_mul_field`, `slope_def_field`, `HasDerivAt.mul` are stated for a general `𝕜`/`𝕜'`.
findings.benefit: Gives reusable `dslope` lemmas not tied to ℂ, usable together with the generalised `taylorCoeffAt` API (e.g. for real-variable use) and as candidates for Mathlib's DSlope file; the ℂ versions follow by instantiation.
